summary: Defines an Instant Messaging identity KeyPurposeId for the Extended Key Usage extension in X.509 v3 certificates, adding to the purposes listed in RFC 5280.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9734 adds a purpose label for X.509 certificates used to prove an instant messaging client's identity. The label helps distinguish these certificates from ones intended for general client or server authentication.

questions: what is an extended key usage for instant messaging
why do im certificates need a key purpose
subtitle: A certificate purpose identifier for credentials that prove an instant messaging client's identity.

tldr.problem: A general certificate purpose such as client or server authentication can create cross-protocol attack risks when used for instant messaging identity.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the Extended Key Usage purpose id-kp-imUri for certificates used to prove an instant messaging client's identity.
tldr.outcome: Issuers can identify certificates intended for this purpose. RFC 9734 is a Proposed Standard and has not been replaced.

today: RFC 9734 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why Instant Messaging Needs a Purpose
sections.content: Instant messaging systems using Messaging Layer Security can use identity certificates for individual clients. A certificate can identify an instant messaging URI or an XMPP URI in its subjectAltName. Organizations may avoid issuing these certificates with a general purpose such as id-kp-clientAuth because a certificate could be abused in a cross-protocol attack.
sections.plainLanguage: A certificate can prove who an instant messaging client is. A separate purpose helps keep that certificate from being treated as a general-purpose login certificate.

sections.title: The id-kp-imUri Purpose
sections.content: The new KeyPurposeId is id-kp-imUri. It may appear in certificates used to prove an instant messaging client's identity. Its object identifier is defined as { id-kp 40 }. The certificate issuer may mark the Extended Key Usage extension as critical or non-critical.
sections.plainLanguage: id-kp-imUri marks a certificate for instant messaging identity. The issuer chooses whether the extension is critical.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations in RFC 5280 apply. The RFC says this purpose does not add new security risks; it reduces existing risk by identifying certificates created to sign instant messaging identity credentials.

Issuers should not combine id-kp-imUri with id-kp-clientAuth or id-kp-serverAuth. Combining them would weaken the specificity provided by the new purpose.
sections.plainLanguage: The purpose is useful when it stays specific. Issuers should not also mark the certificate for general client or server authentication.

sections.title: Registered Identifiers
sections.content: IANA registered decimal 40 for id-kp-imUri in the SMI Security for PKIX Extended Key Purpose registry. It also registered decimal 113 for the ASN.1 module identifier id-mod-im-eku in the SMI Security for PKIX Module Identifier registry.
sections.plainLanguage: The registries assign shared numbers to the new certificate purpose and its ASN.1 module. That lets systems refer to each identifier consistently.
